subject: Re: OEM Core Switching Solution
text:
Hi Shantanu,
Thank you for your interest and for sharing your thoughts on the MII
requirement.

We understand that Make in India (MII) is popular and mandatory for certain
local and government projects, and we are fully open to supporting this
through a structured and practical approach.
Below is our suggested way forward:

1. Specification confirmation & sample testing
Please let us know which specifications or models you are interested in.
We recommend starting with sample testing, which will help you evaluate our
Web UI, operating system, and overall functionality, and also give both
sides a clearer understanding of how MII implementation can be planned
later.

2. TEC / MTCTE certification
We understand that MTCTE (TEC) certification is mandatory for commercial
deployment in India.
Typically, TEC certification is handled by the local Indian entity.
From our side as the OEM, we can fully support the certification process by
providing the required technical documentation, test support, and version
control once the target model is confirmed.
At this early evaluation stage, we suggest not making this the primary
focus yet.

3. MII implementation roadmap
To achieve MII 60%, our usual approach is:
Start with SKD
Move to CKD
Gradually increase localization, including deeper hardware and possible
software-level customization
SKD is usually the easiest first step and also helps you decide how certain
hardware components may be sourced or assembled locally.

To proceed efficiently, we would like to understand:
3.1 Whether you can handle import procedures for complete units, SKD, and
CKD
3.2 Your current thoughts or plans regarding MII implementation, so we can
align our actions accordingly
Once the sample testing and technical evaluation are completed, we can move
into more detailed discussions.

Looking forward to your feedback.
Thank you.
